transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you into the clinic today?

They sent me here. My lieutenant did. Lieutenant Miller... he’s been riding the rigs for like twenty years. He drives this old Ford, you know, the ones with the rust always eating up the wheel wells? My dad had a truck just like that when I was a kid. We used to take it out to the reservoir. Catching sunfish mostly, nothing big. The water always smelled kind of like copper out there, especially in the late summer when the algae gets really thick. 

But anyway, at the station... I was just fixing the airway bags. I kept moving them into a pattern. I knew it was the right pattern, it had to be exactly that way. And I was repeating the dispatch numbers out loud to keep track of it all. Miller came over and told me to stop, to step away from the rig, but I wouldn't. I couldn't. Because if I broke the sequence, the whole bay would go bad. It just felt like the whole place would go completely bad if I stopped moving them. 

You ever notice how those ambulance bays always smell like diesel and bleach? It gets right into the fabric of your uniform. No matter how much detergent you use, you just can't wash it out. My washing machine at home is starting to make this weird clanking noise on the spin cycle, too... but yeah, that's why they told me I had to come here.
How has your sleep been over the past few days?

Sleep? I don’t really know. I haven't really been keeping track of it or anything. I just... I lay down. My mattress is one of those memory foam ones, but it holds the heat way too much. You know how they make those? It’s all polyurethane and chemicals. It's actually the exact same stuff they use for the bench pads in the back of the rigs. We had this one rig, Unit 42, and the suspension was completely shot on it. Every time we hit a pothole over on Elm Street, you’d feel it right in your teeth. Elm Street has the absolute worst potholes, right by that old bakery. They bake sourdough in the middle of the night, and if you drive by at like 4 AM, the whole block smells like vinegar and yeast. I always liked 4 AM, though. The sky gets this weird bruised purple color right before the streetlights finally click off...
Do you feel like your thoughts have been moving much faster than usual?

Faster? I don't know, maybe. I haven't really noticed them speeding up, just... they're just there. Like, I'll be thinking about something, and then I'm thinking about something else. Like the other day, I was thinking about the dispatch radio. The static on it. It’s got this very specific frequency of static, you know? It sounds exactly like the old television we had when I was growing up. The one with the dial you had to actually turn. My brother used to break the dial all the time, so we had to use a pair of pliers to change the channel. We’d sit there watching those old reruns, the ones where the colors were all washed out. The green always looked kind of yellow. Yellow is a terrible color for a wall, by the way. They painted the breakroom at the station yellow last year, and it just makes everyone look sick under those fluorescent lights. The lights hum, too. If you listen close, it’s a B-flat. I learned that in middle school band. I played the trumpet for exactly three weeks before I quit. The brass smelled funny on my hands. Kind of like pennies.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one else was around?

Voices? No, I don't... I mean, I hear the sounds I'm supposed to hear. Like the static on the radio I was telling you about, or the hum of the lights. The lights at the station are one thing, but the ones in my apartment building hallway are even worse. They flicker, just a little bit, like a strobe light but really slow. It drives my neighbor crazy. Mrs. Higgins, she lives in 4B. She’s always complaining about the maintenance guy, Carl. Carl drives this massive snowplow in the winter, even though it barely snows here anymore. The blade on the front of it scrapes the asphalt so loud it sets off car alarms down the whole street. Car alarms are basically useless now, right? Nobody even looks out their window when they go off. They just assume it's a mistake. Like when someone accidentally hits the panic button on their keys while they're carrying groceries. I always buy the paper bags for groceries because the plastic ones end up blowing into the storm drains. The drains get clogged up with leaves and plastic, and then the street floods right by the intersection...

Watching me? Well, yeah, of course they are. I mean, I know the injury review people and some of the supervisors have been watching me through the station cameras. They say it's just routine paperwork, but I know they're changing my triage notes to make me look unsafe. They think I don't notice, but I do. Just like I notice how the cameras have that little red light that blinks when they're recording. It’s the exact same shade of red as the taillights on the new ambulances. The new ones have those LED strips instead of the regular bulbs. They’re so bright they actually hurt your eyes if you stare right at them in the dark. I was staring at them the other night while we were waiting at the hospital bay, and I realized they pulse. Not a steady light, but a fast pulse. It’s supposed to save battery power or something, but it just looks unnatural. Natural light is so much better. Like sunlight coming through a prism. My grandmother had this crystal bird hanging in her kitchen window, and every morning at exactly 7:15, it would cast these tiny rainbows all over the linoleum floor. The linoleum was that awful avocado green color from the 70s. Everyone had that color back then. Even the refrigerators were green...
How long have you felt that your supervisors are watching you and changing your notes?

How long? The camera and the paperwork stuff, and everybody getting all worked up at the station... it's been about two months. Yeah, two months. Right around the time they switched out the coffee machine in the breakroom. They brought in one of those pod things. You know, where you put the little plastic cup in and it punctures the top? It makes this hissing sound when it brews, kind of like a radiator letting off steam. The radiator in my first apartment used to hiss like that all winter. It drove me crazy because it was right next to the bed, and it would wake me up at 3:00 AM. 3:00 AM is the worst time to wake up, because it's too late to go back to sleep but too early to actually get up and do anything. So I'd just lie there and listen to the pipes clanking. The plumbing in that building was terrible. The water always came out brown for the first few seconds when you turned on the tap. You had to let it run before you could brush your teeth. Toothpaste always tastes weird if the water isn't cold enough. I only use the mint kind, though. The cinnamon one burns my gums...
